rules.title: Bounded collections, batched walks
rules.what: Never load an unbounded table with ->get()/findAll(); paginate exposed lists and walk large volumes with chunk(), cursor() or toIterable().
rules.why: Hydrating every row into objects costs memory and CPU proportional to the table, and grows silently with the data.
rules.how: Eloquent: paginate(), chunkById(), lazy(), cursor(); Doctrine: setMaxResults(), toIterable() with periodic clear().

patterns.note: Whole-table load; candidate unless the table is small and bounded by design.

verify.how: A test on a large seeded table shows bounded memory and query count.

rules.title: Eager-load what you walk
rules.what: When a loop reads an association, load it up front (with() in Eloquent, a fetch join in Doctrine); project the useful columns.
rules.why: An association read inside foreach fires one query per element: the N+1 pattern, invisible in the code and obvious in the query log.
rules.how: Model::with('rel')->..., select only needed columns, Doctrine DQL JOIN FETCH; enable Model::preventLazyLoading() outside production.

patterns.note: Loop over a property of an object; check whether it is a lazily loaded association.

verify.how: Query count stays constant as the number of rows grows (debugbar, query log assertion).

rules.title: Bulk writes, existence tests
rules.what: Write in batches (insert(), upsert(), Doctrine batch flush) instead of save() per row; test existence with exists(), not count() > 0.
rules.why: One database round trip per record multiplies latency and server work; a count scans rows an existence test would stop at.
rules.how: Model::insert($rows) or upsert(); flush every N entities then clear(); ->exists().

patterns.note: count() > 0 used as an existence test; exists() stops at the first row.

verify.how: Bulk operation test asserts the number of queries is proportional to batches, not rows.

rules.title: Stream files and exports
rules.what: Read and write large files and exports as streams (fopen + block reads, fputcsv, generators) rather than file_get_contents/file().
rules.why: Loading a whole file costs memory proportional to its size and caps the size the script can handle.
rules.how: fopen/fgets or SplFileObject, yield rows from a generator, StreamedResponse for downloads.

patterns.note: Whole-file read; fine for small config files, candidate for user files and exports.

verify.how: Memory peak (memory_get_peak_usage) stays flat on a file larger than the expected maximum.

rules.title: Index lookups instead of linear search
rules.what: Inside loops, look up by key (isset($index[$k])) instead of in_array()/array_search() over a large array.
rules.why: in_array walks the whole array; repeated per element the work becomes quadratic and collapses on real volumes.
rules.how: Build the index once with array_flip() or array_column(..., null, 'id') before the loop.

patterns.note: Linear search close to a loop header; candidate if the array grows.

verify.how: No linear search over a growing array inside a loop.

rules.title: Shared HTTP client, bounded caches
rules.what: Use one injected HTTP client instead of curl_init() per call; give every file or memory cache an expiry and a purge; enable OPcache in production.
rules.why: A connection per call repeats DNS and TLS; a cache without purge grows storage and backups with dead entries.
rules.how: Inject a Guzzle/Symfony HttpClient service; cache with TTL (APCu, Redis, PSR-6 expiresAfter); opcache.enable=1 and composer dump-autoload -o.

patterns.note: Raw curl handle; check it is not created per request.
File cache write; check expiry and purge.

verify.how: HTTP client is a shared service; each cache write sets a TTL; OPcache enabled in the production image.
